notes:
The threshold here is STRICT (every valid sample must pass), unlike the trajectory gate's 2-of-3. The key-gate suite has now run 6/6 five times over (#180, twice in #187, and the three runs of this baseline: 181s + 264s + 272s, --no-cache), with zero voided samples — it does not flake, so a single failure is signal and must not be absorbed by a threshold. The VOID rules still apply: a judge parse failure or a provider error is re-drawn, never counted as a K-case failure. If this suite ever starts flaking, loosen the threshold deliberately and record why — do not let it drift.

THAT CONDITION HAS NOW BEEN MET, and #189 deliberately did NOT act on it. Under the 36-tool surface (#182) the suite no longer runs clean: over 7 samples per case measured by #189 (one N=3 whole-suite run plus a 4-draw top-up) K1 is 6/7 and K5 is 5/7, while K2/K3a/K3b/K4 stayed 3/3. NO EXPECTATION BELOW WAS MOVED — absorbing those into the baseline is the one edit the policy forbids, and loosening the threshold is a policy change #189's scope excluded. The gate therefore exits non-zero on K1/K5, and that red is a request for a deliberate threshold decision, not a hidden regression. See each case note for the failure shape.

DECISION (2026-08-08, owner, #193): threshold loosened STRICT -> 2-of-3, exactly as the original notes sanctioned. Why: under the 36-tool surface the suite is measurably flaky (K1 6/7, K5 5/7 — new flake shapes, NOT the mechanisms #189 fixed), and a permanently red strict gate costs more signal than it protects. The expectations below are UNCHANGED — no case was absorbed; K1/K5 remain expected PASS and now pass at 2-of-3 on the same evidence. If a case drops below 2-of-3, that is a real regression under the loosened policy. Tightening back to strict requires the same deliberate decision this loosening did.

K1.note: Comprehensive US+EP search with EP gated. #191's routing collapse is FIXED at the mechanism: it used to fold the whole search into one patent_search_subagent call that never saw the key gate (2/4), and #189's delegation limit removed that — zero subagent calls in 14 post-fix runs, and a dedicated 4-draw probe went 4/4. The one residual failure is a DIFFERENT shape: a run that stopped immediately after search_patents returned the gate, never doing the live US office (k1_completed_live_office + k1_did_not_stall_on_the_ask). One sample in seven; it fails the strict threshold.

K2.note: Single EP document read with no EPO OPS key.

K3a.note: CONTROL — the forbid rule must not over-suppress the CN web fallback.

K3b.note: CONTROL — dead US routes with a working key still reach the web fallback.

K4.note: Keyless pivot framed as different data, never as a substitute.

K5.note: Key added mid-conversation: only the gated office re-run. Newly flaky — 3/3 in every prior measurement (#180, #187 twice, #184, #191, and once more inside #189), then 2 failures in 7 samples here. Both are the same slip and neither touches anything #189 changed: the US work landed in the RESUME turn instead of the first one, so k5_delivered_live_office_first and k5_did_not_redo_live_office fail together. Turn placement, not merge doctrine.
